newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga makes early start on North Sea Vigdis oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Saga makes early start on North Sea Vigdis oilfield.

text.p: Norway's largest listed oil company Saga Petroleum ASA said on Wednesday it had started up the Vigdis oilfield in the Norwegian North Sea five months ahead of schedule and 600 million crowns under budget.
The development will add around 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) to Norwegian crude production, which averaged around 3.02 million bpd in 1996, according to the latest figures from the Oil Directorate.
Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag said the Vigdis module began pumping oil to the nearby Snorre platform on Tuesday. From there it would be piped to the Gullfaks A installation for storage and export.
"The oil is in the pipeline between Snorre and Gullfaks. It should reach Gullfaks by 6 p.m. (1700 GMT) tonight," Schibevaag told Reuters.
Saga said modification of Snorre had raised its production capacity to almost 360,000 bpd, making it the world's largest floating production platform.
Vigdis, discovered in 1986, cost 4.5 billion crowns to bring on stream, 12 percent under the original budget of 5.1 billion crowns.
Recoverable reserves are estimated at 29 million cubic metres, or 182 million barrels, of oil. Production life will be around 15 years.
The field comprises three subsea well templates with 12 wells at a water depth of 280 metres.

Partners in Vigdis are operator Saga with 7.7 percent, Den norske stats oljeselskap (Statoil) with 4.4 percent, the Norwegian state's direct financial interest with 51 percent, Esso with 10.5 percent, Idemitsu with 9.6 percent, Norsk Hydro ASA with 8.4 percent, Elf Petroleum with 5.6 percent and Deminex with 2.8 percent.
